players.product: ZT Systems AI rack/system integration for AMD next-generation accelerated compute (Helios), plus AI rack metal fabrication, liquid-cooling manifolds, busbars and high-layer PCBs

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 FY2026 (quarter ended December 27, 2025) revenue was $3.19 billion, up 59% year over year and toward the high end of the outlook, driven by growth in communications networks and cloud and AI infrastructure in the core Sanmina business plus the addition of ZT Systems (only 2 months of ZT Systems included); both core Sanmina and ZT Systems came in near the high end of their outlook ranges. Non-GAAP operating margin was 6.0% (up 40 basis points, the second quarter in a row at 6%) and non-GAAP diluted EPS was $2.38 (up 66.1%), above the outlook.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $3.19 billion, up 59% YoY; non-GAAP operating margin 6.0%; non-GAAP diluted EPS $2.38 (+66.1%)

quarterly_data.signal: Revenue by end market: communication networks, cloud and AI infrastructure came in around 62% of revenue, with the core Sanmina business in this segment growing approximately 20% year over year; the CEO's line reads 'ZTE revenue came for our plan at the high end of our guidance in total of $1.964 billion' (with the other end markets at $1.226 billion, the $1.964 billion reads as the total for this end market, not ZT Systems alone). Industrial, energy, medical, defense and aerospace, automotive and transportation were 38% of revenue or $1.226 billion, down about 3%. Bookings were solid with book-to-bill over 1. Segments: IMS revenue $2.79 billion, up 72% (IMS non-GAAP gross margin 8.7%); CPS revenue $434 million, up 4.3%, with CPS non-GAAP gross margin of 12.9% held back by investments that came online to support new programs expected to deliver margin-accretive growth, plus a few program transitions.
quarterly_data.figure: comms/cloud/AI infrastructure around 62% of revenue, total $1.964 billion; core portion approximately 20% YoY; IMS $2.79 billion, up 72%; CPS $434 million, up 4.3%

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 FY2026 outlook (first full quarter of ZT Systems): revenue $3.1 billion to $3.4 billion (midpoint $3.25 billion = 62% growth year over year), non-GAAP operating margin 5.7% to 6.2% depending on mix, non-GAAP diluted EPS $2.25 to $2.55, capital expenditures around $95 million and depreciation approximately $45 million. The CEO said the core Sanmina business will grow quarter over quarter and double digits year over year and ZT Systems is expected to grow quarter over quarter; core Sanmina is still expected to grow high single digits for the fiscal year. Management guides one quarter at a time.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 revenue $3.1 billion to $3.4 billion; non-GAAP operating margin 5.7% to 6.2%; non-GAAP diluted EPS $2.25 to $2.55; capex around $95 million

quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal 2026 and the ZT Systems transition: asked about the roughly $14 billion consensus, the CEO said 'we believe we have a very good chance of hitting $14 billion.' The CFO restated that back in May Sanmina said it expected a ZT Systems revenue run rate of $5 billion to $6 billion once the transaction closed (annualizing the 2-month Q1 guide gives $5.7 billion), said the business is still going through the transition and 'a lot of the old platforms at this point now have rolled off', and said the accelerated compute opportunity 'really comes towards the end of our calendar -- at the end of calendar 2026.' The CEO said Sanmina is not going to retain all legacy ZT customers but has high confidence the retained customers will grow and new customers will be added; ZT Systems margins are in line with core Sanmina and the deal was immediately accretive to EPS.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 revenue 'a very good chance of hitting $14 billion'; ZT Systems run rate $5 billion to $6 billion ($5.7 billion annualized)

quarterly_data.signal: AI data center strategy: the goal is to double Sanmina's revenue in the next 2 years, and the CEO said the AI opportunities are on track to deliver '$16-plus billion in our calendar year '27'; strong demand for AI hardware is expected in the second half of calendar 2026, 2027 and into 2028, all driven by new platform and new technology projects. Sanmina is pursuing vertical integration for AI data centers 'from components and liquid cooling racks to full system integration at scale'. It has the capacity and power to support present customer demand but keeps investing in AI data center capacity for fiscal 2027 and 2028 requirements: Q1 capex was $87 million, spending will be 'around 90 plus', and '90% of that is really for '27 or '28'. Operating margin is forecast at 5.7% to 6% short term and 6 to 7-plus percent longer term.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue goal: double in the next 2 years; $16-plus billion in calendar year '27; 90% of capex for '27 or '28

quarterly_data.signal: Communications networks and cloud infrastructure: strong demand for high-performance switches and enterprise storage; Sanmina is growing and expanding its optical advanced packaging products business and builds high-performance network systems 'from 400, 800 gig, and we're starting to ship 1.6 terabytes.' Communications demand was very strong in the December quarter and is expected to stay strong in the March quarter and for the rest of the year, and a strong pipeline of new cloud and AI projects is expected to drive growth in the second half of calendar 2026, calendar 2027 and beyond.
quarterly_data.figure: 400, 800 gig systems; starting to ship 1.6 terabytes

quarterly_data.signal: Supply: the CEO said 'we have some material shortages out there around memory and some of the special ASIC customer ASIC but very strong demand' in the communications/networking business.

Energy / power for AI data centers: Sanmina sees strong demand for power products to support AI data centers and is expanding with a new factory in Houston, Texas for its energy business, focused on medium voltage transformers (distribution), grid scale transformers (transmission) and battery storage systems, using its vertical integration (electronics, machining, fabrication, bus bars). It partnered with a company the transcript prints as 'Contra out of Europe, Croatia' to co-design custom medium voltage transformers, has a long-term commitment from a large industry-leading strategic customer and orders already on the books, is ramping the facility now, and plans to ship a few units in late 2026 and be ready for full production in calendar year 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: ship a few units in late 2026; full production in calendar year 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Cash and balance sheet: Q1 cash flow from operations $179 million, capital expenditures $87 million (slightly above outlook) and free cash flow $92 million; ongoing capacity and technology investments are planned in the United States, India and Mexico. Cash was $1.42 billion with no borrowings on the $1.5 billion revolver (liquidity approximately $3.6 billion); inventory net of customer advances was $2.2 billion, up 74% on the ZT Systems acquisition (inventory turns 5.3x); non-GAAP pretax ROIC 32.1%; net leverage 0.8x against a long-term target of 1.0x to 2.0x, which management expects to reach over time as it invests in working capital for ZT Systems growth. Repurchased 516,000 shares for approximately $79 million, with approximately $160 million remaining on the program.
quarterly_data.figure: CFO $179 million; capex $87 million; FCF $92 million; liquidity approximately $3.6 billion; inventory $2.2 billion (up 74%); net leverage 0.8x

connects_to.relationship: ZT Systems builds AMD next-generation accelerated compute (Helios) racks/systems; pre-production validation with AMD and joint hyperscale/OEM customers

contracts.signal: CEO: 'opportunities utilizing AMD partnership is huge for us and all the investments being made to be able to support future required.' Sanmina is positioning for 'the new product, new platforms that are going to be coming up in the end of the fiscal year and calendar year and we're investing for that'; the CFO said the accelerated compute opportunity comes 'at the end of calendar 2026' as old ZT Systems platforms have rolled off.
contracts.type: manufacturing partnership / next-generation system integration ramp
